meta.notes: Facts used by the troubleshooting and care articles (Phase 6b): where tanks leak, the maintenance schedule manufacturers publish, anode rod rules and parts prices, the checks for no hot water, the reset button (ECO), noises, running out of hot water and the rotten egg smell. Every figure is quoted from the reference named in its record; all references were opened on the date in 'checked'. Parts prices are retailer listing prices on that date and change often. Nothing here is our own measurement.

aos-manual.title: Residential Gas Water Heater: Installation Instructions and Use & Care Guide (document 100400765)
quotes: Drain and flush tank, clean condensate pan, and remove and inspect anode rod after first six months of operation and at least annually thereafter.
Depending on the hardness of your water, repeat this process at least annually, or more frequently if needed.
Failure to drain and flush the water heater of sediment can deteriorate the tank and drain valve and cause leaks resulting in property damage.
Note that sediment in the bottom of the tank may clog the valve and prevent it from draining. If you cannot get the tank to drain, contact a qualified person.
Allow a hot water faucet to run full for at least three minutes to make sure the tank has all the air removed and is completely full of water.
It may take an hour or more for the tank of cold water to heat up.
If you use a water softener, your anode rod will deplete faster than normal.
Anode rods are a consumable item and are not covered under warranty.
A small amount of water dripping from the Temperature and Pressure (T&P) Relief Valve usually means the home's water pressure is too high and/or you need a Thermal Expansion Tank.
Install a Pressure Reducing Valve (PRV) on the main cold water supply line. Adjust the PRV to between 50 and 60 psi.
Do not cap or plug the T&P Relief Valve or discharge pipe, and do not operate the water heater without a functioning T&P Relief Valve; this could cause an explosion.
If the T&P Relief Valve is discharging large amounts of very hot water, turn the gas supply valve off and call a qualified person.

When a gas water heater is first lit and the tank is cold, condensation often forms inside the water heater... Condensation is not a leak and will go away once the tank reaches normal operating temperature.
If you have no hot water after two hours, refer to the Troubleshooting Section.
Plumbing Leak. Even a small leak in the hot water side of the home's plumbing system can make it appear that the water heater is producing little to no hot water.

Harmless bacteria normally present in tap water can multiply in water heaters and give off a 'rotten egg' smell... the standard anode rod ... can be replaced with a special zinc anode rod which may help reduce or eliminate the odor.
To protect the tank, an anode rod must be installed in the water heater at all times or the warranty is void.
WHAT TO DO IF YOU SMELL GAS: Do not try to light any appliance. Do not touch any electrical switch; do not use any phone in your building. Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.
The 'HOT' setting sets the water temperature to approximately 120°F, reducing the risk of scald injury.
Most codes allow a maximum incoming water pressure of 80 psi (we recommend a working pressure no higher than 50-60 psi).
Connect the water pressure gauge to an outside faucet and measure the maximum water pressure experienced throughout a 24-hour period (highest water pressures often occur at night).
Install a metal drain pan... Install an automatic leak detection... device.
Apply thread sealant tape or pipe joint compound and reinstall the anode rod tightly using a 1-1/16" socket wrench with an extension.

An odorant is added by the gas supplier to the gas used by this water heater. This odorant may fade over an extended period of time. Do not depend upon this odorant as an indication of leaking gas. We recommend installing a fuel gas and carbon monoxide detector.
This water heater has a resettable thermal switch installed as part of the FVIR system. Do not attempt to disable or modify this feature in any way.
If the tank is full of cold water, condensation may form inside the water heater. This condensation may drop on the burner causing a sizzling sound.

Hydrogen gas builds up in a hot water system when it is not used for a long period (two weeks or more). Hydrogen gas is extremely flammable. If the hot water system has not been used for two weeks or more, open a hot water faucet for several minutes at the kitchen sink before using any electrical appliances connected to the hot water system. If hydrogen is present there will probably be an unusual sound such as 'air' escaping through the pipe as hot water begins to flow.
Lighting label: PRESS / HOLD KNOB IN POSITION. PRESS IGNITER BUTTON UNTIL PILOT LIGHTS. RELEASE KNOB WHEN STATUS LIGHT BLINKS.

aos-leaking.title: What to do when your hot water heater is leaking
quotes: Wipe the area completely dry with towels, then watch for new moisture. If it reappears within a few hours, you have a leak.
Leaks typically develop at four points on your tank.
Tank water heaters hold 30-80 gallons, and a more serious leak can flood your home in a matter of hours.
Water pressure above 80 PSI can turn a small crack into a gushing leak.
Most residential tanks take 20-30 minutes to empty.
Water soaking into drywall, flooring, or insulation creates mold growth within 24-48 hours.
Electric Water Heater Leaks: Failed gaskets around heating elements cause water to seep from the side of the tank where elements penetrate through the steel.
Gas Water Heater Leaks: Moisture near the burner assembly or gas line connection requires immediate professional help since water can interfere with combustion and create carbon monoxide risks.

aos-leak-guide.title: Water heater leaking: causes, signs and fixes
quotes: The anode rod, or 'sacrificial' rod, corrodes over time to protect the tank from rusting. These rods usually last 3-5 years before they need to be replaced.
If the T&P valve is leaking due to high pressure, turning down the thermostat could stop the leak. The addition of a properly sized and charged expansion tank is the solution to this issue.
A water leak coming from the base of the heater is often the first indication of a serious problem.

aos-not-working.title: Water heater not working? Common problems and fixes
quotes: A very common reason for an electric water heater not working is a tripped circuit breaker.
Thermostat Issues: Causes temperature inconsistencies and can trip the high-limit safety switch (red reset button), often due to a grounded heating element or a faulty lower thermostat.
Gas Supply Problems: Prevents burner ignition and can also cause the pilot to extinguish.
Plan your showers around recovery time: gas tanks need 30-40 minutes, electric tanks need 60-90 minutes.
Electric Water Heaters: Turn off power at the circuit breaker before touching anything.
If you smell rotten eggs or suspect a gas leak for any reason, turn off the gas supply valve immediately and call a professional.
Check water pressure, which should be 50-60 PSI and no higher than 80 PSI, and install a thermal expansion tank.

Fix: Flush the water heater with a solution of water and hydrogen peroxide. For persistent issues, increase the water temperature to 140 degrees F for a short period to kill bacteria, then return to a safer temperature. Install mixing valves to prevent scalding. Alternatively, installing an aluminum/zinc composite anode rod can also help eliminate odor-causing bacteria.

Gas Water Heaters: If you smell rotten eggs or suspect a gas leak for any reason, turn off the gas supply valve immediately and call a professional—don't continue to troubleshoot and don't try to diagnose the problem yourself.

How do I reset an electric water heater? To reset an electric water heater, first turn off power at the circuit breaker. Remove the access panel covering the upper thermostat to locate the red reset button (Energy Cut Off). Press the reset button firmly until you hear it click.
If the button trips repeatedly or you're uncomfortable performing these steps, contact a professional as repeated tripping indicates serious problems like shorted elements or faulty thermostats.

aos-maintenance.title: Water heater maintenance (draining, flushing, anode rod, T&P valve)
quotes: Most types of tank water heaters require flushing at least once per year. If you live in a hard water area, you may need to flush your water heater more often.
Ideally, you should turn your water heater off for a few hours before draining the tank.
For an electric water heater, it is critical to make sure the tank is full before turning the power back on.
A rod in good working condition should be smooth and around a half inch in diameter. If the sacrificial anode rod shows signs of deterioration or has several inches of exposed core wire, replace it.
How long an anode rod will last depends on what chemicals are in the water, how much hot water is used, and whether or not a water softener is installed.
The T&P valve should be inspected once a year by the consumer and every 5 years by a professional.

aos-checklist.title: Water heater maintenance checklist
quotes: Have your hot water heater serviced once a year. If you have hard water in your area, get it serviced twice a year since mineral buildup happens faster.
Tankless models skip these tasks but need descaling, which means flushing out mineral deposits that build up inside the unit where water gets heated.
Once the rod's mostly gone or 6 inches of core wire is exposed, your tank starts rusting from the inside out.

ge-anode.title: Water heater: anode rod maintenance and service
quotes: The anode rod must be removed from the water heater's tank and inspected annually, and replaced when more than 6" (15.2 cm) of core wire is exposed at either end of the rod.
Please be aware that artificially-softened water will cause the anode rod to consume more rapidly.
Operation with the anode rod removed will shorten the life of the glass-lined tank and will void warranty coverage.
Some areas have water conditions that may cause an odor to develop in the water heater. Special alloy replacement rods are available to address the condition.
Failure to replace the anode rod when consumed voids the warranty for the tank.

rinnai-flush.title: 13-step tankless water heater flushing procedure
quotes: It's important to flush those mineral deposits at least once a year.
Use 4 gallons (15.1 liters) of undiluted white vinegar to clean your tankless water heater. Never use chemical solutions of any kind.
This procedure may take up to 45 minutes.

cpsc-scald.title: Avoiding Tap Water Scalds (Publication 5098)
quotes: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) urges all users to lower their water heaters to 120 degrees Fahrenheit.
Most adults will suffer third-degree burns if exposed to 150 degree water for two seconds.

rheem-lifespan.title: Water heater lifespan: when to repair vs. replace (March 25, 2026)
quotes: Flush the tank annually; replace the anode rod every 3-4 years; aim for 40-60 psi.
If the leak is from the tank itself, replacement is usually required.

corro-protec.title: How a powered anode rod works
quotes: Unlike traditional rods, which sacrifice themselves, they use a small electrical current to prevent corrosion.
Diagram of a standard powered anode rod with power supply, indicator light.

rinnai-tb.title: Technical Bulletin TB-188: Sensei enhanced flush procedure
quotes: When unit has finished draining, remove the in-line filter at the cold water inlet and clean out any residue.
Clean filters immediately after flush is complete.

aos-electric-manual.title: Residential Electronic Thermostat Electric Water Heater: Installation Instructions and Use & Care Guide (document 2000598248)
quotes: The Energy Cut Off (ECO) shuts off power to the water heater's elements if the temperature of the water in the tank gets too hot. If the ECO has tripped, you'll have no hot water.

A tripped ECO can usually be reset, but you should have a qualified person investigate the cause of the overheating and repair the problem. Do not turn the power back on until the cause of the overheating has been identified and repaired.
The ECO was tripped if you hear a click when it is reset. In most cases, a tripped ECO indicates that the tank overheated due to a problem with one of the elements or thermostats
The ECO was not tripped if you didn't hear a click. In that case, the thermostats should be checked by a qualified person.

If the Temperature and Pressure Relief Valve (T&P Valve) releases large amounts of very hot water, it is likely due to a shorted heating element, or more rarely a non functioning thermostat, or the thermostat does not fit snuggly against the tank. Very high water temperatures can also cause the Energy Cut Off (ECO) to trip
Undersized water heater. If your water heater runs out of hot water too quickly, it may be too small for your needs. If the water heater is old, consider replacing it with a larger model.

you may be able to meet your family's hot water needs with the existing water heater by installing Thermostatic Mixing Valves at each point-of-use and then turning the thermostat(s) to a higher setting.
You can also reduce your home's hot water needs by washing clothes in cold water, installing flow restrictors on shower heads, repairing leaky faucets, and taking other conservation steps.

If the lower heating element is not working, you will have some hot water but not as much as before. Because the lower element does most of the work, the lower element usually wears out before the upper element.

Although eliminating the bacteria that causes 'smelly water' with a Chlorination system is the only sure treatment, in some cases, the standard anode rod ... can be replaced with a special zinc anode rod which may help reduce or eliminate the odor.
In cases where the 'rotten egg' smell is pronounced, you can raise the tank temperature to 140°F in order to reduce bacteria growth in the tank.
Low supply voltage

ge-eco.title: Water Heater - Energy Cut Off Control (ECO)
quotes: If for any reason the water temperature becomes excessively high, the high limit control (ECO) breaks the power circuit to the heating element. Once the control opens, it must be reset manually. Resetting of the high limit control should only be done by a qualified service technician.
The cause of the high temperature condition must be investigated by a qualified service technician and corrective action must be taken before placing the water heater in service again.

aos-noise.title: Why your water heater might be making noise
quotes: Popping starts when steam bubbles force their way through mineral deposits stuck at the bottom of your tank.

crackling can also be caused by aluminum hydroxide, jelly-like beads that form when an aluminum anode rod reacts with chlorine in your water. If you see green, blue, or gray beads when flushing your tank, ask your plumber about switching to an aluminum-zinc anode rod.
Humming sounds usually come from loose parts vibrating as your water heater runs.
If you have an ultra-low NOx water heater, humming may indicate a damaged burner rather than loose parts.

Whistling happens when water squeezes through a space that's too small such as a valve that's partly closed, a clogged pressure relief valve, or sediment blocking the normal flow. Mechanical screeching comes from worn-out parts. In gas water heaters, blower motor bearings wear down. In electric tanks, heating elements get damaged and start making noise.
Heat trap nipples ... can also tick or click as hot water expands and contracts inside them during heating cycles.
Drain and flush your tank once a year to remove sediment buildup. Flush every six months if you have hard water.
If you've flushed the tank but the sounds continue, something inside has likely failed and needs repair.

aos-noise-guide.title: What to do when your hot water heater is making noises
quotes: If your water heater is knocking, it's likely water slamming into the heater's internal shutoff valves too quickly. Installing a water hammer arrestor adds a bit of shock absorption to your heater.
If your water heater has a blower, this may be a case of a dirty blower wheel or obstructed vent.

Turn off the water heater and wait for it to cool. Then work from top to bottom, tightening screws and pressing on joints to spot any unexpected gaps or movement. Anything beyond basic tightening, such as a rusted joint or weak panel, should be left to a professional.
Flushing your tank can be helpful both diagnostically (visible sediment that comes out with the flush is a definite red flag) and as a solution for random noises.

rheem-noise.title: The ultimate guide to water heater noises: what's normal (and what isn't) (June 10, 2026)
quotes: Ticking or clicking: Often caused by heat traps or pipe expansion as temperatures change
Humming: Common in electric units when heating elements are active
Gurgling: Normal water movement after periods of heavy use
Soft ignition sounds: Typical in gas-powered systems
The short answer is: Yes, a hissing, sizzling or dripping water heater can be dangerous.
Water dripping onto a hot burner (gas models)
A leaking heating element gasket (electric models)
A water heater banging, rumbling or knocking often points to an issue in your plumbing system rather than the heater itself.
Sudden valve or faucet closure; Excessively high water pressure; Loose or unsecured pipes
If you hear hissing, sizzling or persistent screeching, it's safest to turn off the unit and contact a professional.
A unit that's 8–12+ years old

aos-reheat.title: How long for a water heater to reheat?
quotes: The recovery rate for gas tanks typically runs 40-50 gallons per hour.
Electric models typically recover 15-20 gallons per hour.
In winter, water entering your home might be 40-50°F. In summer, it could be 60-70°F.
This seasonal difference can add 15-30 minutes to winter recovery times compared to summer.
A 40-gallon tank might have a 60-gallon first hour rating because it combines stored hot water with the water it heats during that hour.

aos-heat-up.title: How long does it take a water heater to heat up?
quotes: Electric water heaters rely on two heating elements—lose one and your recovery time doubles since you're operating at half capacity.
Sediment sitting at the bottom of your tank acts like a blanket between the heat source and your water.
A water heater that takes longer to heat up each year most likely has failing heating elements that need replacement.

stiebel-sizing.title: Tankless sizing sheet: size a model for your location
quotes: Table based on output temp and flow rate of 1.5 GPM at 105°F for shower, 1 GPM at 105°F for kitchen sink, 0.5 GPM at 90°F for bathroom faucet.
WATER HEATER SETTINGS OF 120˚F ARE MIXED WITH COLD WATER AT THE TAP

psu-h2s.title: Hydrogen sulfide (rotten egg odor) in water wells
quotes: Sometimes, hydrogen sulfide may be noticeable only in the hot water in the home. In this case, chemical reactions within the water heater may be the source of the rotten egg odor.
The magnesium rod can chemically reduce sulfates to form hydrogen sulfide.

Removal could cause increased corrosion and reduced life of the hot water heater and will likely void the manufacturer's warranty. Replacement of the magnesium rod with an aluminum rod should eliminate the rotten egg odor while maintaining corrosion protection for the heater.
Most people can detect hydrogen sulfide levels well below 0.5 mg/L.
Although sulfur-reducing bacteria can impart taste and odor in the water, they do not cause human health concerns.
When the water contains a small hydrogen sulfide concentration, less than about 1.0 mg/L, activated carbon filtration may be effective.
it is normally not used when hydrogen sulfide concentrations exceed about 2 mg/ L.
Oxidizing filters can remove up to 2-3 mg/ L of hydrogen sulfide.
Chlorination can be used to remove any level of hydrogen sulfide, but it is most often applied in cases where the hydrogen sulfide concentration exceeds 6.0 mg/L.
Testing for hydrogen sulfide must be done in the home, or the sample must be chemically stabilized before being sent to a commercial testing lab.
In most cases, sulfur-reducing bacteria and hydrogen sulfide odor will return quickly after shock chlorination.

kcc-gas.title: Natural gas safety
quotes: Gas in its pure state is odorless. That is why gas companies add a chemical called Mercaptan, so it can be easily identified. Mercaptan contains sulfur, which is what makes it smell like rotten eggs.
If you smell gas, stop what you are doing and leave the area immediately.
Once you are in a safe location, call your utility company or 911. Do not re-enter until a gas company employee says it is ok.

aos-water-quality.title: Residential guide to monitoring your water quality
quotes: Hard water is in more than 85% of American homes, and hard water scale is a leading cause of failure for tankless water heaters.
Scale buildup may reduce the efficiency of your water heater ... and may cause overheating and damage to the point where the water heater could begin to leak water.

safety.gasSmell: If you smell gas, do not light anything, do not touch electrical switches or use a phone in the building, and call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.
safety.powerOff: On an electric water heater, turn the power off at the circuit breaker before you touch anything.

leakPoints.caption: Where a tank water heater leaks, what it usually means, and what fixes it

rows.where: Pipe connections on top of the tank
rows.cause: Loose or corroded fittings on the hot outlet or cold inlet

rows.where: Relief valve on the side or top, or its discharge pipe
rows.cause: Water pressure too high, thermal expansion, debris in the valve, or a failed valve
rows.fix: Check pressure, add an expansion tank, replace a failed valve (never plug it)

rows.cause: Valve not fully closed, worn washer, or a failed valve
rows.fix: Close it fully; replace the valve if it keeps dripping

rows.where: Side of an electric tank, at an element
rows.cause: Failed heating element gasket
rows.fix: Power off, drain, replace the gasket or element

rows.where: Around the burner of a gas tank
rows.cause: Condensation on a cold tank, or water reaching the burner from a leak above
rows.fix: Condensation clears as the tank heats; any other water near the burner needs a professional

rows.where: Tank bottom or a wet tank body
rows.cause: Steel tank corroded through
rows.fix: None: the tank cannot be repaired

leakPoints.source: A. O. Smith leaking guide, troubleshooting page and Use & Care Guide (100400765); Rheem

flushSchedule.caption: How often to flush, by water heater type and water (manufacturer guidance)

rows.after: At least once a year, more often with hard water
rows.also: Inspect the anode rod; operate the relief valve per its label

rows.after: At least once a year, more often with hard water
rows.also: Inspect the anode rod; refill fully before power goes back on
Inspect the anode more often: softened water uses it up faster

rows.after: Descale at least once a year

flushSchedule.source: A. O. Smith Use & Care Guide (100400765) and maintenance checklist; GE Appliances; Rinnai; Rinnai TB-188 (inlet filter)

anodeTypes.caption: Replacement anode rod types and listing prices

rows.good: One of the three standard rod metals A. O. Smith names
rows.watch: If the hot water smells of rotten eggs, makers suggest a special alloy rod instead

rows.good: One of the three standard rod metals A. O. Smith names
rows.watch: Use the metal and size your manual specifies for your model

rows.good: Rotten-egg smell: the special rod A. O. Smith and GE point to
rows.watch: May reduce or end the smell; A. O. Smith says killing the bacteria is the only sure fix

rows.good: Made of linked sections instead of one solid rod
rows.watch: Check thread size and length against your tank's manual

noHotByType.caption: No hot water: the first things to check, by type

rows.first: The breaker in your panel (a very common cause)
rows.then: The red reset button (high-limit switch) behind the upper panel, with the power off
rows.pro: The breaker or reset trips again, or an element or thermostat has failed

rows.first: That the gas valve is open and the control knob is not on Off or Vacation
rows.then: Whether the pilot is lit; relight only by the label on the heater
rows.pro: The pilot will not stay lit, or you smell gas

rows.first: The status light on the gas control
rows.then: Its flash code in the manual; a lockout can clear after a wait
rows.pro: The code points to a sensor, igniter or venting fault

rows.first: The error code on the display, and that the gas or power is on
rows.then: Whether the inlet filter is blocked or scale is due to be flushed
rows.pro: The code repeats after a reset or names a part

rows.first: Other taps: if they are hot, the heater is fine
rows.then: That tap's mixing valve (common in shower controls)
rows.pro: The valve needs replacing and you are not comfortable doing it

noHotByType.source: A. O. Smith troubleshooting page and Use & Care Guide (100400765)

resetCauses.caption: Why an electric water heater reset button (ECO) trips

rows.cause: A shorted or grounded heating element
rows.clue: Trips again soon after a reset; the breaker may trip too; the relief valve may release a lot of very hot water

rows.cause: A thermostat stuck on, or not pressed tight against the tank
rows.clue: Water gets hotter than the setting before the button trips
rows.who: Qualified person: replace or refit the thermostat

rows.cause: Loose or damaged wiring
rows.clue: The breaker trips as well; only found by testing the wiring with the power off

rows.cause: The ECO did not trip at all
rows.clue: No click when you press the button, and still no hot water

rows.cause: No power reaching the heater
rows.clue: The reset button is fine but nothing heats; a tripped breaker is the most common cause
rows.who: You (breaker, once); electrician if it trips again

resetCauses.source: A. O. Smith electric Use & Care Guide (2000598248) and troubleshooting page

noiseSounds.caption: Water heater noises: what each sound usually means

rows.cause: Heat traps or pipes expanding as they warm and cool

rows.sound: Soft whoosh when a gas burner lights
rows.cause: Normal ignition
Elements heating, or a loose part vibrating
rows.todo: If it is loud, turn the heater off, let it cool, tighten loose screws

rows.cause: Water moving after heavy use, or trapped air
rows.todo: Nothing, unless it comes with other signs

rows.cause: Sediment on the tank bottom trapping steam bubbles
rows.todo: Drain and flush; if it continues after a flush, have it inspected

rows.sound: Crackling, with green, blue or gray jelly beads in the drain water
rows.cause: Aluminum hydroxide from an aluminum anode reacting with chlorine
rows.todo: Flush; ask about an aluminum-zinc anode

rows.sound: Sizzling when a gas heater first fires on a cold tank
rows.cause: Condensation dripping on the burner
rows.normal: Yes, if it stops once the tank is hot

rows.sound: Hissing or sizzling that keeps going
rows.cause: A leak dripping onto the burner, or a leaking element gasket
rows.todo: Turn the heater off at the gas valve or breaker and have it inspected

rows.cause: A partly closed valve, sediment, or a relief valve problem; worn blower bearings (power-vent gas); a damaged element
rows.todo: Open the water valves fully; if it continues, have it inspected

rows.sound: Banging or knocking when a tap shuts
rows.cause: Water hammer, high water pressure, loose pipes
rows.todo: Water hammer arrestor; pressure-reducing valve; secure pipes

rows.sound: Air rushing out of a hot tap after two weeks or more unused
rows.cause: Hydrogen gas built up in the hot water system
rows.todo: No flames or sparks nearby; run the kitchen hot tap for several minutes

noiseSounds.source: Rheem noise guide (June 2026); A. O. Smith noise pages; A. O. Smith gas Use & Care Guide (100400765)

runsOutCauses.caption: Hot water runs out fast: causes, clues and fixes

rows.cause: The heater is too small for your busiest hour
rows.clue: It runs out at the same point every busy morning, and always has
rows.fix: Check the size you need; mixing valves plus a higher setting; or a bigger unit

rows.cause: Colder incoming water in winter
rows.clue: Fine in summer, short in winter
rows.fix: Expected; size for winter, or use less hot water per shower

rows.cause: Lower heating element failed (electric)
rows.clue: Some hot water, but much less than before; slow to recover

rows.cause: Sediment on the tank bottom
rows.clue: Popping or rumbling; a slow decline over months

rows.cause: Melted or broken dip tube, or reversed connections
rows.clue: Started soon after an install or soldering work; water turns lukewarm fast
rows.fix: Replace the dip tube or correct the connections

rows.cause: Thermostat set too low, or failing
rows.clue: Water is never very hot, even at the start
rows.fix: Raise the setting (with mixing valves above the CPSC level); replace a failed thermostat

rows.cause: A faulty mixing valve in one shower
rows.clue: Only that shower runs short; other taps stay hot

rows.cause: A leak on the hot side of the plumbing
rows.clue: The burner or elements run almost all the time

rows.cause: Tankless: too many taps at once
rows.clue: Temperature drops when a second shower or the washer starts
rows.fix: Spread out use, or check the unit's size

runsOutCauses.source: A. O. Smith electric and gas Use & Care Guides; A. O. Smith reheat and heat-up pages

smellSources.caption: Rotten egg smell: where you notice it and what it means

rows.where: In the air near the water heater, the stove or a gas line
rows.cause: Possible natural gas leak: gas companies add a sulfur odorant that smells like rotten eggs
rows.todo: Leave now; call the gas utility or 911 from outside; do not switch anything on or off

rows.cause: Bacteria in the tank reacting with the anode rod to make hydrogen sulfide
rows.todo: Heater fix: flush, change the anode metal, heat to the higher setting for a while, or chlorinate

rows.where: Hot and cold water, on a private well
rows.cause: Hydrogen sulfide in the groundwater
rows.todo: Test the water; whole-house treatment sized to the result

rows.where: Hot and cold water, on city water
rows.cause: The supply, not the heater

smellSources.source: Kansas Corporation Commission; A. O. Smith Use & Care Guides; Penn State Extension

h2sTreatment.caption: Whole-house treatment for well water with hydrogen sulfide, by level

rows.upkeep: Low running cost; higher purchase price

rows.range: Any level; usual choice above 6.0 mg/L

h2sTreatment.source: Penn State Extension, Hydrogen sulfide (rotten egg odor) in water wells
